Curl Brackets Check

curl_bracket_check.Rd

Verify that all the bodies of the if, else, for, while, repeat and function (including lambda \(x)) constructs of a function are delimited by curly brackets { }. For instance: if(x > 1){ base::return(x) } and not if(x > 1) base::return(x). The safer-r rule requires curly brackets for every body, even single-statement ones.

Usage

curl_bracket_check(
  x,
  export = FALSE,
  out_path = ".",
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

x

a function name, written without quotes and brackets.

export

Single logical value. Export the modified function into a .R file (see the out_path argument)? If TRUE, the modified function is not returned but only exported. An error is returned if the file already exists in out_path, and if the tested function is not designated by a function name (like test or package::test), i.e., written by an inline definition (like function(x){x}) or by a component writing (like FUN_LIST$fun). If FALSE (default), the modified function is returned by the function instead of being exported.

out_path

Single character string indicating the absolute pathway of the folder where to export the modified function file, named <FUNCTION_NAME>_safer.R (e.g., mean_safer.R). out_path = "." (default) means the R working directory set by the user. Ignored if the export argument is FALSE.

safer_check

Single logical value. Perform some "safer" checks? If TRUE, checkings are performed before main code running (see the safer-r project): 1) correct lib_path argument value 2) required functions and related packages effectively present in local R libraries and 3) R classical operators (like "<-") not overwritten by another package because of the R scope. Must be set to FALSE if this function is used inside another "safer" function to avoid pointless multiple checkings.

lib_path

Vector of characters specifying the absolute pathways of the directories containing the required packages for the function, if not in the default directories. Useful when R packages are not installed in the default directories because of lack of admin rights. More precisely, lib_path is passed through the new argument of .libPaths() so that the new library paths are unique(c(new, .Library.site, .Library)). Warning: .libPaths() is restored to the initial paths, after function execution. Ignored if NULL (default) or if the safer_check argument is FALSE: only the pathways specified by the current .libPaths() are used for package calling.

error_text

Single character string used to add information in error messages returned by the function, notably if the function is inside other functions, which is practical for debugging. Example: error_text = " INSIDE <PACKAGE_1>::<FUNCTION_1> INSIDE <PACKAGE_2>::<FUNCTION_2>.". If NULL, converted into "".

Value

If the export argument is FALSE: the modified function, i.e., the submitted function with all the missing curly brackets { } added, returned by base::return(). NULL is returned if no modification was done, i.e., if the submitted function was already compliant.

If the export argument is TRUE: the modified function is written into the <FUNCTION_NAME>_safer.R file of the out_path directory and NULL is returned (invisibly), with a message indicating where the modified function has been exported. If no modification was done, no file is written and NULL is also returned.

In both cases, a table-like text message indicating the missing curly brackets { } is printed, or a message saying that everything seems fine.

Table-like: column 1, the line number in the function code (starting at the "<- function" line, i.e., without counting the #' header lines); column 2, the construct (if, else, for, while, repeat or function); column 3, the code preceding the construct body.

Details

The result is used to modify the code inside the tested function like this: { <CODE> }.

More precisely, curl_bracket_check() verifies that the first code element of the body of each if, else, for, while, repeat and function construct (after the () of the condition or of the arguments, when present) is a curly bracket {. Comments are ignored during this verification.

In else if chains, an else part followed by an if() construct is not reported, because the chained if() is checked on its own. When the modified function is built (see the returns section), such an else if() construct is left unmodified (only the else is not modified): the chained if() construct itself is modified on its own.

Function bodies reduced to a single .Primitive(...) call are skipped, because primitive functions cannot be delimited by curly brackets. For instance, the body of base::`+` is .Primitive("+") and is not reported. Contrary to these ones, UseMethod(...) bodies are reported (e.g., base::mean).

When the modified function is built, the curly brackets { } are added as follows: a { followed by a space is inserted before the first character of the construct body, and a space followed by a } is inserted after the last character of the construct body. Comments located between the construct keyword and the body (e.g., if(x > 1) # comment) are kept before the added opening bracket. If the body contains a comment between statements, like if(x > 1) x # comment followed by + 1 on the next line, the added closing bracket is inserted at the end of the last code line of the body, i.e., after the comment. The added curly brackets are always separated from the body content by a single space, and the original code formatting is otherwise left unchanged. Warning: because the curly brackets are added around the construct body, code lines can become longer than 80 characters: check the modified function with a linter if needed.

When the modified function is built, it is validated by re-parsing the modified code: if the modified code cannot be parsed, an internal error is returned (please, report it in the link given by the error message). Note that the line numbers of the reported missing curly brackets (column 1 of the table-like message) are those of the submitted function, before modification.

When the export argument is TRUE, the exported file contains the code of the modified function obtained with base::deparse(): comments of the submitted function are lost in this file (this is a known limitation of base::deparse()). The returned modified function (when export = FALSE) preserves the comments of the submitted function. The exported file contains an assignment of the modified function (<FUNCTION_NAME>_safer <- function(...) ...), so that base::source()ing it recreates the modified function. Warning: the tested function must be designated by a function name (like test or package::test) when export = TRUE: an inline definition (like function(x){x}) or a component writing (like FUN_LIST$fun) returns an error, because the name of the exported file could not be determined reliably.

Warning: curl_bracket_check() cannot check constructs written with backquotes, like `if`(x > 1, base::return(x), base::return(0)). Please, use the standard writing.

The returned line numbers are indicative, depending on which source is checked. For instance, saferDev::colons_check (compiled) has not the same line numbers as its source file. Notably, compiled functions do not have comments anymore, compared to the same source function sourced into the working environment. In addition, the counting starts at the "<- function" line, i.e., without counting the #' header lines potentially present in source files.

Examples

# Warning: these examples may not work well when using the "Run examples" link 
# because of a particular environment. Please, copy-paste in a local environment.
# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/curl_bracket_check.html
fun1 <- function(x){ if(x > 1){ base::return(x) } else { base::return(0) } }
saferDev::curl_bracket_check(fun1)
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::curl_bracket_check().
#> INSIDE fun1(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
fun2 <- function(x){ if(x > 1) base::return(x) } ; saferDev::curl_bracket_check(fun2)
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2(), SOME CURLY BRACKETS {} ARE MISSING AFTER:
#> 
#> LINE	CONSTRUCT		CODE
#> 3	if		if (x > 1) 
#> 
#> function (x) 
#> {
#>     if (x > 1) {
#>         base::return(x)
#>     }
#> }
#> <environment: 0x564c11f2eda8>
fun2 <- function(x){ if(x > 1) base::return(x) } ; fun2_safer <- saferDev::curl_bracket_check(fun2) ; fun2_safer(2)
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2(), SOME CURLY BRACKETS {} ARE MISSING AFTER:
#> 
#> LINE	CONSTRUCT		CODE
#> 3	if		if (x > 1) 
#> 
#> [1] 2
fun2_ter <- function(x){ if(x > 1) base::return(x) } ; saferDev::curl_bracket_check(x = fun2_ter, export = TRUE, out_path = ".") # fun2_ter_safer.R written in the working directory, NULL returned
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2_ter(), SOME CURLY BRACKETS {} ARE MISSING AFTER:
#> 
#> LINE	CONSTRUCT		CODE
#> 3	if		if (x > 1) 
#> 
#> MODIFIED CODE EXPORTED IN:
#> ./fun2_ter_safer.R
#> 
#> NULL
saferDev::curl_bracket_check(mean)
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE mean(), SOME CURLY BRACKETS {} ARE MISSING AFTER:
#> 
#> LINE	CONSTRUCT		CODE
#> 1	function		function (x, ...) 
#> 
#> function (x, ...) 
#> {
#>     UseMethod("mean")
#> }
#> <environment: namespace:base>
